source.title: Interpretability in Parameter Space: Minimizing Mechanistic Description Length with Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition
source.authors: Dan Braun; Lucius Bushnaq; S. Heimersheim; Jake Mendel; Lee Sharkey

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling. The training-details appendix says the TMS40−10 dataset uses 5 input features, which conflicts with the stated 40-feature setting.
record.tranche_reason: Applies a new parameter-decomposition method to toy superposition networks and measures whether learned components correspond to their feature directions; it does not reproduce the original study's full geometry or sparsity-transition measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports MMCS and ML2R for APD components in two TMS settings, plus qualitative neuron-contribution results in compressed-computation models. It does not sweep sparsity or feature importance, test LLMs, or measure SAE feature stability. Scrubbed/anti-scrubbed loss comparisons validate APD component specialization but do not directly measure a listed version's geometry or capacity account, so they are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper uses toy superposition models as ground-truth testbeds for its decomposition method (APD). Its reported numbers (MMCS, ML2R, neuron-contribution match, scrubbing losses) measure how well APD components match the target model. They do not measure whether or how superposition arises. It does not vary sparsity, measure angles between features, manipulate feature importance, or test LLMs or SAEs. The compressed-computation models show neurons shared across 100 functions with 50 neurons, but no capacity or importance account is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude APD identifies ground-truth mechanisms in toy models (features in superposition, compressed computations, cross-layer distributed representations) up to small error and shrinkage. They add that APD is currently limited to toy models by computational cost and hyperparameter sensitivity, and that its gradient attributions need improving.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses the Toy Model of Superposition setup but applies attribution-based parameter decomposition and evaluates component-to-weight-column alignment; it does not reproduce the original study's sparsity and feature-geometry sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The TMS5−2 result required using attributions from the APD model rather than the target model; the authors say the small-dimensional setting was brittle. They report that batch top-k and loss-term coefficients can significantly influence APD outcomes in other experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: A trained 1-layer residual MLP computes 100 ReLU functions with 50 neurons, outperforming a monosemantic baseline, with neurons contributing to multiple functions. The authors suspect this may be less sparsity-dependent than superposition but could not establish it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Toy networks can perform compressed computation (more nonlinear functions than neurons), possibly distinct from sparsity-dependent computation in superposition.

record.problems: The relevant superposition evidence is from toy networks and one reported feature probability, with no sparsity sweep or direct measurement of angles among feature directions. The 5-feature/2-dimension result is described as brittle. The TMS40−10 training-details appendix contains an apparent feature-count inconsistency.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant version-bearing result rows omitted. The paper's scrubbed/anti-scrubbed and sparse-forward-pass loss comparisons, and its hand-coded gated-function experiment, were not extracted because they do not directly measure the listed geometry or capacity-account versions.

untested.parts: All parts. No sparsity sweep, phase transition, or geometry measurement. The TMS target models are only training targets for APD; the pentagon in Fig. 3 is shown illustratively.
All parts. Feature importance is not varied, and there is no test of dedicated versus shared dimensions.
All parts. No LLMs are studied.
All parts. SAE limitations are discussed from the literature only.
All parts. Rank-1 TMS mechanisms are assumed by construction. Multidimensional mechanisms are discussed but left for future work.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation and tranche (tests/T2) are overturned to uses_without_test/T4. All numeric results measure APD's fidelity to target models whose superposition is assumed. The paper's authors overlap with superposition theory work but it is not an original source. The feature-count inconsistency the record flags (appendix says 5 features for TMS40−10) appears to be a copy error. The TMS5−2 result needed a special attribution adjustment and is described as brittle.

versions.untested_parts: No sparsity sweep or sparsity-dependent transition; no direct measurement of angles among feature directions, regular polygon geometry, or feature importance.
The study shows shared neuron contributions in toy compressed-computation models, but does not test whether feature importance determines which features get dedicated dimensions or share.
No test of polysemantic neurons arising without capacity pressure.
No LLM feature-spread or SAE recovery experiments.
The paper discusses concerns about sparse dictionary learning, but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical.
Tests rank-1 parameter mechanisms corresponding to input features in TMS, not whether features are one-dimensional across other models or settings.

rows.subject: TMS5−2
rows.operation_detail: Measured the best-matching APD component-column direction against each target-model weight column (MMCS).
rows.measure: Mean max cosine similarity (MMCS) between target weight columns and corresponding columns of their best-matching APD components
rows.note: The paper says this near-1 MMCS indicates APD components are close geometric representations of the target model's feature directions. This is component-to-target alignment, not a measurement of angles between different feature directions.
rows.check: MMCS compares APD component columns with target weight columns. It scores the study's own method, not superposition geometry or feature dimensionality. The rank-1 structure is the authors' definition of ground truth, not a finding.

rows.subject: TMS5−2
rows.operation_detail: Measured the magnitude ratio of each target weight column to its best-matching APD component column (ML2R).
rows.measure: Mean L2 ratio (ML2R) of matching APD component-column magnitudes to target weight-column magnitudes
rows.note: The authors describe this as shrinkage relative to the target weights; it does not measure feature-direction angles.
rows.check: ML2R measures APD component shrinkage relative to target weights. It is method performance and says nothing about V1.

rows.subject: TMS40−10
rows.operation_detail: Measured the best-matching APD component-column direction against each target-model weight column (MMCS).
rows.measure: Mean max cosine similarity (MMCS) between target weight columns and corresponding columns of their best-matching APD components
rows.note: The paper says this near-1 MMCS indicates APD components are close geometric representations of the target model's feature directions. The paper describes the TMS ground-truth mechanisms as rank 1, one per input feature.
rows.check: Same as R1: alignment of APD components to target columns, not a measure of superposition. The rank-1 mechanism is assumed by construction.

rows.subject: TMS40−10
rows.operation_detail: Measured the magnitude ratio of each target weight column to its best-matching APD component column (ML2R).
rows.measure: Mean L2 ratio (ML2R) of matching APD component-column magnitudes to target weight-column magnitudes
rows.note: The authors describe this as shrinkage relative to the target weights; it does not measure feature-direction angles.
rows.check: Same as R2: APD shrinkage, i.e. method performance.

rows.subject: 1-layer residual MLP
rows.size_stated: 100 input features; 50 MLP neurons; residual stream width 1000
rows.operation_detail: Measured neuron contributions to each input-feature computation in the target model.
rows.measure: Neuron contribution values, defined from the neuron's input read and output influence for each feature computation
rows.note: The text describes the target as computing 100 functions with 50 neurons and shows neurons contributing to multiple feature computations. No numeric contribution values are stated in the text.
rows.check: This is a figure of target-model neuron contributions used as the reference for APD. It shows neurons shared across feature computations, but there is no importance manipulation and no test of a capacity account. The authors suspect the solution may not depend on sparsity and call it 'compressed computation' rather than superposition. It belongs under fits_no_version, not V2.

rows.subject: 2-layer residual MLP
rows.size_stated: 100 input features; 50 MLP neurons split across two layers; residual stream width 1000
rows.operation_detail: Measured neuron contributions to each input-feature computation across both MLP layers.
rows.measure: Neuron contribution values across the two MLP layers
rows.note: The text describes a 100-function task with 50 neurons and reports computations distributed across both MLP layers; no numeric contribution values are stated.
rows.check: Same as R5, for the 2-layer model. It is a figure-only reference for APD evaluation, with no test of the capacity account.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
